class.name: DisDesignatorPdu
class.brief_description: Designator PDU (type 24): a laser designator spot.
class.description: A Designator PDU describes a laser designator: which entity designates, which entity is designated, the laser code, power and wavelength, and where the spot is, both as an offset from the designated entity and as a geocentric location. The spot's motion is given by a dead reckoning algorithm and a linear acceleration. It is 88 bytes and has protocol family 6 (Distributed Emission Regeneration). godot-dis encodes and decodes the PDU; it does not model the laser or its detection. The PDU is encoded with godot-dis's own code.

link.title: Emissions: radars, jammers, designators and IFF

method.name: decode
method.description: Parses [param bytes] as a Designator PDU and returns it. Returns [code]null[/code] and sets [method DisPdu.get_last_error] if [param bytes] is not a valid Designator PDU (header shorter than 12 bytes, wrong PDU type, protocol version outside 1-7, length field larger than [code]bytes.size()[/code], or fewer than 88 bytes). A length field of 0 is replaced by the datagram size. Bytes after the last known field, up to the length field, are kept in [member DisPduBase.trailing_bytes].

members.member: Designator code name (16-bit, SISO-REF-010 "Designator System Name").
ID of the entity the laser spot is on, as a [Vector3i] ([code]x[/code] = site, [code]y[/code] = application, [code]z[/code] = entity number). [member spot_offset] is relative to this entity.
ID of the entity that holds the designator, as a [Vector3i] ([code]x[/code] = site, [code]y[/code] = application, [code]z[/code] = entity number).
Laser code (16-bit): the pulse code a seeker has to match.
Dead reckoning algorithm used for the spot (8-bit, SISO-REF-010 "Dead Reckoning Algorithm"), with [member spot_linear_acceleration].
Laser power in watts (32-bit float on the wire).
Linear acceleration of the spot in metres per second squared, used by the dead reckoning algorithm (32-bit floats on the wire).

Location of the spot in WGS84 geocentric (ECEF) coordinates, as a [PackedFloat64Array] [code][x, y, z][/code] in metres. Setting an array that does not have exactly 3 values prints an error and leaves the old value.
Position of the spot in metres relative to the designated entity, in that entity's body axes (32-bit floats on the wire).
Laser wavelength in micrometres (32-bit float on the wire).
